mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4.5%, it indicates tighter monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in >40% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3pp increase in unemployment signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in >40% of cases when UNRATE increases.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth indicates weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth slows but SPX returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing industrial production growth signals supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth slows but SPX returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: CPI increases paired with high FEDFUNDS signal inflation and tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPI and FEDFUNDS conditions are met but SPX returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment suggests economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If employment increases but SPX returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, slowing GDP and rising unemployment signal weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth slows and UNRATE rises
failure_condition: If GDP slows and unemployment rises but SPX returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing housing starts indicate weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts slow but SPX returns remain positive.
